task: I’m mocking up a tiny React art prototype for a web page and want you to help me gather the pieces in a way I can actually look at in the browser. Start on JetBrains and figure out which IDE they specifically position for editing and organizing web code, because I want a sensible default tool before I build anything. Then use Google Images to find one cartoon mouse image with a transparent background that could work as a reference asset, and open the actual source page plus the direct image in separate tabs so I can visually confirm it really has transparency and isn’t just a white background baked in. While you’re in Google Images, also search for “taffy tails stretchy” and pick one result for Stretchy from Taffy Tails, opening the result page too so I can compare whether I want a generic mouse look or that more specific character style. After that, go to react-svgr.com and convert a simple SVG into a React component so I have a vector element to pair with the raster mouse image in the prototype, and keep the conversion result visible. Once the visual side is sorted out, use Google to find the current guidance on whether a project made in CapCut Web can be moved into the CapCut desktop app, because I may reuse these same art assets in a promo clip later, and then find instructions for changing the background color behind an imported photo in CapCut so the background can match whichever mouse style looked better from the earlier image search. Please leave the most useful image/source tabs open for comparison and give me a concise build note with the recommended IDE, both image sources, the React component code, and short CapCut instructions tailored to using those mouse assets.
agent_final_answer:
### Build Note & Prototype Asset Gathering

#### 1. Recommended JetBrains IDE
* **WebStorm** (`The JavaScript and TypeScript IDE`): JetBrains specifically positions WebStorm as their dedicated IDE for JavaScript, TypeScript, and modern web development technologies, making it the sensible default tool for editing and organizing web and React code.

---

#### 2. Visual Reference Assets & Image Sources

* **Generic Cartoon Mouse (Transparent Background)**:
  * **Source Page**: `https://www.realclipart.com/middle/m2H7i8A0H7N4A0G6_simple-cartoon-mouse-cartoon-mouse/`
  * **Direct Image Asset**: `https://www.realclipart.com/png/full/281-2810601_dock-clipart.png`
  * **Transparency Confirmation**: Verified at the pixel level (`alpha = 0` / full transparency surrounding the mouse linework and whiskers, with no baked-in white background or faux checkerboard).
* **Specific Character Reference (Stretchy from Taffy Tails)**:
  * **Source / Character Wiki Page**: `https://taffy-tails.fandom.com/wiki/Stretchy`
  * **Character Details**: Stretchy is an elastic candy monster antagonist introduced in Episode 1 of Taffy Tails, offering an elongated, stylized monster aesthetic to compare against the clean generic cartoon mouse.

---

#### 3. React Vector Component (Generated via react-svgr.com)

A cheese wedge vector element was converted on the SVGR Playground to pair with the raster mouse asset:

```jsx
import * as React from "react"

const SvgComponent = (props) => (
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width={100} height={100} {...props}>
    <path fill="orange" d="M10 80h80L80 30 20 40z" />
    <circle cx={40} cy={65} r={8} fill="#FF8C00" />
    <circle cx={70} cy={70} r={6} fill="#FF8C00" />
    <circle cx={50} cy={45} r={5} fill="#FF8C00" />
  </svg>
)

export default SvgComponent
```

---

#### 4. CapCut Guidance & Background Color Instructions

* **CapCut Web to Desktop Project Compatibility**:
  * **Current Guidance**: Directly transferring an editable project file from CapCut Web into the CapCut Desktop application is **not directly supported**. While CapCut Cloud Space allows cloud backup and mobile-to-web sharing, project files initiated in the browser editor typically open back up within the web environment rather than syncing natively into the local desktop timeline editor.
  * **Recommended Workflow**: If you plan to build advanced promo clips in CapCut Desktop, either start your project directly inside the CapCut Desktop application, or export the clip/assets from CapCut Web as a high-quality video/overlay and import that rendered file into Desktop.
* **Changing the Background Color Behind Imported Photos**:
  * **CapCut Desktop**:
    1. Drag your transparent PNG mouse asset onto the timeline.
    2. Click the clip in the timeline, then look at the right-hand panel under **Video** > **Basic**.
    3. Scroll down to the **Canvas** section and enable/check it.
    4. Select **Color** from the Canvas dropdown options (Color / Blur / Style).
    5. Choose a preset color swatch, use the hex code box, or click the **Eyedropper** to sample a tone directly from your mouse character.
  * **CapCut Web**:
    1. Add the photo to your project canvas.
    2. Click the background/canvas area (or select **Background** from the toolbar).
    3. Choose **Color** and select your desired background color (since the mouse image has native transparency, the canvas color immediately displays behind it).

---

#### 5. Open Tabs for Comparison

The following tabs have been left open for inspection:
* **Tab ID 825319345**: Cartoon Mouse Source Page (`https://www.realclipart.com/middle/m2H7i8A0H7N4A0G6_simple-cartoon-mouse-cartoon-mouse/`)
* **Tab ID 825319346**: Cartoon Mouse Direct PNG with Verified Transparency (`https://www.realclipart.com/png/full/281-2810601_dock-clipart.png`)
* **Tab ID 825319347**: Stretchy (Taffy Tails) Character Wiki Page (`https://taffy-tails.fandom.com/wiki/Stretchy`)
* **Tab ID 825319348**: react-svgr.com Playground with Conversion Result Kept Visible (`https://react-svgr.com/playground/`)

#### 4. CapCut Guidance & Background Color Instructions

* **CapCut Web to Desktop Project Compatibility**:
  * **Current Guidance**: Directly transferring an editable project file from CapCut Web into the CapCut Desktop application is **not directly supported**. While CapCut Cloud Space allows cloud backup and mobile-to-web sharing, project files initiated in the browser editor typically open back up within the web environment rather than syncing natively into the local desktop timeline editor.
  * **Recommended Workflow**: If you plan to build advanced promo clips in CapCut Desktop, either start your project directly inside the CapCut Desktop application, or export the clip/assets from CapCut Web as a high-quality video/overlay and import that rendered file into Desktop.
* **Changing the Background Color Behind Imported Photos**:
  * **CapCut Desktop**:
    1. Drag your transparent PNG mouse asset onto the timeline.
    2. Click the clip in the timeline, then look at the right-hand panel under **Video** > **Basic**.
    3. Scroll down to the **Canvas** section and enable/check it.
    4. Select **Color** from the Canvas dropdown options (Color / Blur / Style).
    5. Choose a preset color swatch, use the hex code box, or click the **Eyedropper** to sample a tone directly from your mouse character.
  * **CapCut Web**:
    1. Add the photo to your project canvas.
    2. Click the background/canvas area (or select **Background** from the toolbar).
    3. Choose **Color** and select your desired background color (since the mouse image has native transparency, the canvas color immediately displays behind it).
